slides.title: Is it true?
slides.text: A claim is something you say is true, like: the plant grows about 2 cm a day. Evidence is the data that backs it up.
slides.alt: The bean plant measured each day: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 cm. Dot asks: is this claim supported by the chart?

focus.cue: The evidence: the plant measured each day
Day 5: 10 cm, about 2 cm more each day

slides.title: Enough data?
slides.text: Two bars are a hunch, not a case. When there is too little data, the honest answer is: we cannot tell yet.
slides.alt: Two days of data and a big claim: it will be 20 cm tall by day 10. Supported, not supported, or can't tell yet?

focus.cue: Only two days of data: is it enough?
The honest answer: can’t tell yet

slides.title: Predict the plant
slides.text: The plant grows 2 cm every day. So day 6 will most likely be 2 cm taller than day 5.
slides.alt: Days 1 to 5 grow 2 cm each, up to 10 cm, and the prediction slider for day 6 is set to 12 cm.

focus.cue: Days 1 to 5 grew 2 cm a day, so: 12 cm

slides.title: Say only what it shows
slides.text: Bikes were counted every morning. Thursday has the tallest bar, so the claim that Friday is the busiest day is not supported. And the chart never says why: it only shows how many.
slides.alt: Bikes counted each morning: Thursday's bar is tallest at 15. Dot says the chart goes against the claim that Friday is busiest.

words.means: the data that backs up a claim
use data to say what will happen next

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Data Detective at Clues & Claims and solve all 6 cases. Before you pin a claim, ask: does the chart really show it, or can we not tell yet?
slides.alt: The bean plant measured each day: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 cm. Dot asks: is this claim supported by the chart?

focus.cue: Read the chart before you pin
Does it really show the claim?
